sections.heading: What is Cart Abandonment Rate?
paragraphs: Cart Abandonment Rate measures the percentage of online shoppers who add items to their shopping cart but leave before completing the purchase. It's a critical ecommerce metric that reveals friction in your checkout process, pricing concerns, or trust issues. According to Baymard Institute, the average documented online cart abandonment rate is 70.22% based on 50 different studies.

sections.heading: Why is Cart Abandonment Rate Important?

bullets.label: Revenue Impact
bullets.text: Ecommerce stores lose roughly $18 billion annually due to cart abandonment

bullets.label: Checkout Optimization
bullets.text: Identifies friction points in your purchase flow

bullets.label: Customer Experience
bullets.text: Reveals gaps in trust, pricing, or UX that drive customers away

bullets.label: Marketing ROI
bullets.text: High abandonment wastes acquisition spend. You're paying for traffic that doesn't convert

bullets.label: Recovery Opportunities
bullets.text: Cart recovery emails can recapture ~10% of lost revenue

sections.heading: How to Calculate Cart Abandonment Rate
paragraphs: Example: If 1,000 shopping carts are created and only 300 complete checkout:
sections.formula: Abandonment Rate = ((Carts Created - Carts Completed) / Carts Created) × 100

bullets.label: Show All Costs Upfront
bullets.text: 1. Display shipping, taxes, and fees on product pages, not at checkout

bullets.label: Enable Guest Checkout
bullets.text: 2. 26% abandon because of mandatory account creation

bullets.label: Add Trust Badges
bullets.text: 3. Display security seals and payment icons prominently

bullets.label: Simplify Checkout
bullets.text: 4. Keep it under 3 steps; use address auto-fill

bullets.label: Send Recovery Emails
bullets.text: 5. Abandoned cart emails can recover ~10% of lost orders

bullets.label: Offer Multiple Payment Options
bullets.text: 6. Include digital wallets, BNPL, and local methods
